clue.text: Relative of their barn owl is ousted

indicators.note: ousted means thrown out of place, so the letters of their barn owl are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's family member is evicted along with the barn owl living in their barn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is ousted' reads as the main verb of the sentence, but 'ousted' is the anagram signal working on all twelve letters of 'their barn owl'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sister's husband or a spouse's brother is a relation by marriage, so a relative.

clue.text: Lay to rest in Greater Manchester town

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to put a body in a grave
second meaning: ..., a town north of Manchester in England

explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a market town in the county of Greater Manchester, in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to inter a corpse, and the same spelling names an English town famous for black pudding.

clue.text: Propane exploded? In theory

indicators.note: exploded means blown apart, so the letters of propane are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: Did the propane gas blow up? Only hypothetically.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true on paper holds in principle or as written, but not necessarily in practice.

clue.text: Bad place offering initial salutation

parts.note: hell is the worst place of all

indicators.note: initial picks out the first letter of the word offering

parts.note: the word offering supplies its opening letter

explanation.surface: A nasty spot gives the first greeting a visitor hears.
explanation.definitionFit: Hello is the standard word of greeting, which is what a salutation is.

clue.text: Most unusual Sartre novel

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so the letters of Sartre take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A book by Jean-Paul Sartre that is his strangest work.
explanation.walkthrough: Sartre was a novelist, so 'novel' poses as a noun about his book; it is really the adjective signalling a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarest is the superlative of rare, meaning least common or seldom found.

clue.text: Gear in new Renault

indicators.note: new tells us to make fresh letters from the name Renault

explanation.surface: A gear setting on a brand-new Renault car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' looks like it describes the car but signals a rearrangement of RENAULT. The car surface makes 'Gear' look like car parts in general; it is the specific gear position.
explanation.definitionFit: Neutral is the gearbox position in which no gear is engaged, so the engine drives nothing.

clue.text: Arrange with odd ally in gang

indicators.note: odd says to take the first, third, fifth letters and so on of ally in gang

parts.note: the phrase whose odd-placed letters, read in order, spell out the answer

explanation.surface: Organise things together with a peculiar partner in a criminal gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' looks like it describes the ally, but it picks the odd-numbered letters of the whole phrase 'ally in gang'.
explanation.definitionFit: To align things is to set them in a line or proper order, which is arranging them.

clue.text: Had no food around end of June? Quite the opposite!

definitions.note: the definition: the opposite of having no food, i.e. having eaten lavishly; a verb phrase, like the answer

indicators.note: around means the first part is wrapped about the letter that follows

parts.note: to have fasted is to have gone without eating

indicators.note: end of takes the last letter of the word June

parts.note: the month whose last letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone skipped meals until late June, then joked that they did the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps FASTED (Had no food) about E, from 'end of' June. The exclamation then says the answer means the opposite of 'Had no food', so the definition rides on the wordplay's own words.
explanation.definitionFit: Having feasted means having eaten a large lavish meal, the reverse of going hungry.

clue.text: Drive away the Spanish salesman first

indicators.note: first says the salesman's piece comes before the Spanish word, though the clue gives it later

parts.note: rep is short for representative, a travelling salesman
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: A Spanish salesman is the first to be chased off.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel attackers is to force them back, which is driving them away.

clue.text: Shattered tureen I put together again

indicators.note: a shattered dish is in pieces, so the letters of tureen and I are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone glues a broken soup tureen back together.
explanation.definitionFit: To reunite is to bring parts or people back into union after separation.

clue.text: Ties eventually removed by cook?

parts.note: a cook unties the cords of a kitchen garment at the end of the day; the phrase also means the bonds a grown child eventually cuts with their mother

explanation.walkthrough: To be tied to your mother's apron strings is to depend on her; cutting them means growing independent. The cook literally removes these ties after cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the cords that fasten a kitchen pinafore, and figuratively the bonds of maternal dependence.

clue.text: Snobbish, like a poster?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: conceited, looking down on others
second meaning: a poster is literally fixed up on a wall

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful literal reading: a poster is glued up on the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuck-up is informal for haughty, and read literally it describes a notice fastened up on display.

clue.text: Fish for trout cooked black inside

indicators.note: inside says the black letter goes within the cooked trout
cooked suggests the trout is prepared and so its letters mixed up

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A recipe for trout with something charred in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' turns TROUT into TUROT, and 'inside' puts B (black) within it.
explanation.definitionFit: The turbot is a large European flatfish prized as food.

clue.text: Love to set up French friend with Japanese art

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
to rig is to set up, as with equipment or a stage
ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: A romantic arranges a French friend's introduction to a Japanese craft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' looks like a reversal signal in a down clue, but here it is simply the synonym RIG.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the traditional Japanese craft of folding paper into shapes.

clue.text: Run out of special power — drink up!

indicators.note: up in drink up signals that the letters of the whole run are turned back to front

parts.note: ESP is extrasensory perception, a supposed psychic power
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Your superpower has run out, so finish your drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drink up' looks like a toast, but 'up' reverses both pieces together: ESPALE read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that elapses passes or expires, as a deadline does when it runs out.

clue.text: Forecast public relations order

parts.note: an edict is an official order or decree

explanation.surface: A publicity team issues a ruling about the weather outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: To predict is to say in advance what will happen, the verb sense of forecast.

clue.text: Composes legal actions in English? On the contrary

indicators.note: in on its own would put the legal actions inside the English letter
On the contrary flips that, so the English letter goes inside the legal actions instead

parts.note: writs are legal documents ordering or starting an action

explanation.surface: A lawyer drafts lawsuits in English, or perhaps the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: Read plainly, 'in' would put WRITS inside E, which is impossible; 'On the contrary' reverses the containment so E goes within WRITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who writes music or prose composes it, the verb in the same third-person form.

clue.text: Visitor kept one diagram for good writer

indicators.note: kept means held inside, so the visitor contains the other pieces

parts.note: a caller is someone who pays a visit
I is the Roman numeral for one
a graph is a chart or diagram

explanation.surface: A guest hangs on to a single chart, useful for a fine penman.
explanation.definitionFit: A calligrapher practises the art of beautiful handwriting, so is literally a good writer of letters.

clue.text: No-hoper changing roles

indicators.note: changing says the letters of roles swap places

explanation.surface: A failed actor keeps switching parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A loser is someone habitually unsuccessful, which is what a no-hoper is.

clue.text: A top spinning round one in courtyard

indicators.note: round says the spun letters go around the one
spinning, like a whirling top, shows the letters of a top being churned

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A child's spinning top whirls around someone in a yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning' rearranges A and TOP into PATO, and 'round' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A patio is a paved open area beside a house, Spanish in origin for an inner courtyard.

clue.text: One taking advantage of carouser? Not half!

indicators.note: not half means one half of the eight-letter word carouser is dropped, here its first four letters

explanation.surface: Someone who exploits a heavy drinker, or so the exclamation suggests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is also British slang for 'very much so', disguising the instruction to drop half of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is someone who exploits others for their own gain.

clue.text: Social climber on high at the beginning

parts.note: up means aloft, on high
start means the beginning

explanation.surface: An ambitious newcomer is at the top right from the off.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is someone who has risen suddenly in rank and behaves arrogantly, a parvenu.

clue.text: I sort out threesomes

indicators.note: sort out suggests reorganising, so out signals that the letters of I sort are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone declares they will organise groups of three.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort out' reads as one phrase, but 'sort' is fodder and only 'out' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is a group of three people or things, so trios are threesomes.

clue.text: Railway buff educates clay worker

parts.note: to train someone is to educate or instruct them
a potter shapes clay into pots

explanation.surface: A railway enthusiast who teaches pottery classes.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainspotter is a hobbyist who logs locomotive numbers, a railway enthusiast.
